citation: Öz-Alkoyak, H., & Vuran, S. (2025). Otizmli çocuklara kavram öğretiminde dağıtılmış ve sıklaştırılmış uygulamalar [Distributed and massed practices in teaching concepts to children with autism]. Ankara Üniversitesi Eğitim Bilimleri Fakültesi Özel Eğitim Dergisi, 26(3), 331-345. https://doi.org/10.21565/ozelegitimdergisi.1464202
notes:
REAL published case, participant 'Emre' (1 of 4 in the study), digitized from Figure 2 (Şekil 2, p. 339) — the daily-probe-session correct-response-count graph, filled squares = distributed practice (Dağıtılmış, here condition A), open circles = massed practice (Sıklaştırılmış, condition B). Open access under CC-BY-NC-ND (stated on the article's first page); values extracted for research replication purposes, not the figure image itself.

How this was digitized: NOT run through PlotDigitizer — read visually, point by point, from a 400dpi render of the published figure by Claude (an AI assistant), cropped and re-examined for precision. Each session's raw score (0-9, the paper states 9 trials per daily probe session) was read off the y-axis to the nearest visible gridline/marker position and converted to a proportion (raw/9) for this CSV's 0-1 'value' column; n=9 throughout, matching the paper's stated 9 trials/probe.

Honesty caveats, explicitly: (1) this is a visual estimate by an AI, not a precision pixel-coordinate tool — treat individual values as approximate, not exact; (2) only the DISTRIBUTED-condition series (A) is densely covered across the intervention phase; the MASSED-condition series (B) has only 4 visible points in Emre's panel specifically (at sessions 13, 18, 23, 28) — this sparsity looks consistent with the study's design (massed sessions occurred far less often per week than distributed ones, per the paper's Figure 1/Şekil 1: 4 distributed teaching days/week vs 1 massed day/week) and with the other 3 children's panels showing the same lopsided pattern, but a masked/overlapping point at y=0 near the x-axis could have been missed; (3) baseline-phase points (sessions 1-3, before either teaching condition began) were deliberately excluded from this CSV — the replay harness is meant to test the same 'watch results and stop early' logic AURA itself uses, which only starts once teaching begins, not before; (4) this covers only 1 of the study's 4 participants (Emre) — the paper reports all 4 met the mastery criterion under distributed practice and none did under massed, so 'A' is used as reference_winner for this participant specifically. A human should re-verify these values against the actual figure (ideally with real PlotDigitizer) before this case is cited in any publication.
